Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-6026", "title": "Diabetes in Children and Teens", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Until recently, the common type of diabetes in children and teens was type 1 ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "With Type 1 diabetes, the pancreas does not make insulin."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Insulin is a hormone that helps glucose,or sugar, get into your cells to give them energy."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Without insulin, too much sugar stays in the blood."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Now younger people are also getting type 2 diabetes ."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Type 2 diabetes used to be called adult-onset diabetes."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "But now it is becoming more common in children and teens, due to more obesity ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "With Type 2 diabetes, the body does not make or use insulin well."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Children have a higher risk of type 2 diabetes if they are overweight or have obesity, have a family history of diabetes, or are not active."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Children who are African American, Hispanic, Native American/Alaska Native, Asian American, or Pacific Islander also have a higher risk."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "To lower the risk of type 2 diabetes in children: Have them maintain a healthy weight Be sure they are physically active Have them eat smaller portions of healthy foods Limit time with the TV, computer, and video Children and teens with type 1 diabetes may need to take insulin."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Type 2 diabetes may be controlled with diet and exercise ."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "If not, patients will need to take oral diabetes medicines or insulin."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "A blood test called the A1C can check on how you are managing your diabetes."}]}, {"id": "MLP-379", "title": "Radiation Exposure", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "It travels in the form of energy waves or high-speed particles."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Radiation can occur naturally or be man-made."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "There are two types: Non-ionizing radiation, which includes radio waves, cell phones, microwaves, infrared radiation and visible light Ionizing radiation, which includes ultraviolet radiation, radon , x-rays , and gamma rays What are the sources of radiation exposure?"}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Background radiation is all around us all the time."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Most of it forms naturally from minerals."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "These radioactive minerals are in the ground, soil, water, and even our bodies."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Background radiation can also come from outer space and the sun."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Other sources are man-made, such as x-rays, radiation therapy to treat cancer, and electrical power lines."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "What are the health effects of radiation exposure?"}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Radiation has been around us throughout our evolution."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "So our bodies are designed to deal with the low levels we're exposed to every day."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "But too much radiation can damage tissues by changing cell structure and damaging DNA."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "This can cause serious health problems, including cancer."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "The amount of damage that exposure to radiation can cause depends on several factors, including: The type of radiation The dose (amount) of radiation How you were exposed, such as through skin contact, swallowing or breathing it in, or having rays pass through your body Where the radiation concentrates in the body and how long it stays there How sensitive your body is to radiation."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "A fetus is most vulnerable to the effects of radiation."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Infants, children, older adults, pregnant women, and people with compromised immune systems are more vulnerable to health effects than healthy adults."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Being exposed to a lot of radiation over a short period of time, such as from a radiation emergency , can cause skin burns ."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "It may also lead to acute radiation syndrome (ARS, or \"radiation sickness\")."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "The symptoms of ARS include headache and diarrhea."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Those symptoms will go away and the person will seem healthy for a little while."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "How soon they get sick again, which symptoms they have, and how sick they get depends on the amount of radiation they received."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "In some cases, ARS causes death in the following days or weeks."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Exposure to low levels of radiation in the environment does not cause immediate health effects."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "But it can slightly increase your overall risk of cancer."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "What are the treatments for acute radiation sickness?"}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Before they start treatment, health care professionals need to figure out how much radiation your body absorbed."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "They will ask about your symptoms, do blood tests, and may use a device that measures radiation."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "They also try get more information about the exposure, such as what type of radiation it was, how far away you were from the source of the radiation, and how long you were exposed."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Treatment focuses on reducing and treating infections, preventing dehydration , and treating injuries and burns."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Some people may need treatments that help the bone marrow recover its function."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "If you were exposed to certain types of radiation, your provider may give you a treatment that limits or removes the contamination that is inside your body."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "You may also get treatments for your symptoms."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "How can radiation exposure be prevented?"}, {"id": "S033", "text": "There are steps you can take to prevent or reduce radiation exposure: If your health care provider recommends a test that uses radiation, ask about its risks and benefits."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "In some cases, you may be able to have a different test that does not use radiation."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "But if you do need a test that uses radiation, do some research into the local imaging facilities."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Find one that monitors and uses techniques to reduce the doses they are giving patients."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Reduce electromagnetic radiation exposure from your cell phone."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "At this time, scientific evidence has not found a link between cell phone use and health problems in humans."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "But if you still have concerns, you can reduce how much time you spend on your phone."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "You can also use speaker mode or a headset to place more distance between your head and the cell phone."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "If you live in a house, test the radon levels, and if you need to, get a radon reduction system."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "During a radiation emergency, get inside a building to take shelter."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "Stay inside, with all of the windows and doors shut."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Stay tuned to and follow the advice of emergency responders and officials."}]}, {"id": "MLP-1262", "title": "Hodgkin Lymphoma", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Hodgkin lymphoma, also called Hodgkin disease, is a type of cancer that develops in the lymph system."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Your lymph system is part of your immune system ."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It helps protect your body from infection and disease."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "The lymph system is made up of tissues and organs that produce, store, and carry white blood cells."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It includes your: Bone marrow Lymph nodes Lymphatic vessels Spleen Thymus Tonsils Hodgkin lymphoma is one of the main types of lymphoma ."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Each type starts in different types of white blood cells."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The cause of Hodgkin lymphoma is unknown."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "But there are certain people who are at higher risk of developing it."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Who is more likely to develop Hodgkin lymphoma?"}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Certain factors can make you more likely to develop Hodgkin lymphoma: Age."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Hodgkin lymphoma is most common in early adulthood (age 20-39 years) and in late adulthood (age 65 years and older)."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "The risk of adult Hodgkin lymphoma is slightly higher in males than in females."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Past Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Having an infection with EBV as a young child or teenager increases your risk of Hodgkin lymphoma."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Having a parent or sibling with Hodgkin lymphoma increases your risk of developing it."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "What are the symptoms of Hodgkin lymphoma?"}, {"id": "S016", "text": "The signs and symptoms of Hodgkin lymphoma may include: Painless, swollen lymph nodes in the neck, underarm, or groin Fever for no known reason Drenching night sweats (very heavy sweating during sleep) Weight loss for no known reason in the past 6 months Itchy skin, especially after bathing or drinking alcohol Fatigue How is Hodgkin lymphoma diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S017", "text": "To find out if you have Hodgkin lymphoma, your provider: Will ask about your symptoms and medical history."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "This will include checking for signs of disease, such as lumps or anything else that seems unusual."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "May order some lab tests, such as: Complete blood count Blood chemistry studies Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) test Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) test Blood tests to rule out other medical conditions May do imaging tests such as a CT and PET (positron emission tomography) scans May do a lymph node biopsy What are the treatments for Hodgkin lymphoma?"}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Treatments for Hodgkin lymphoma include: Chemotherapy Radiation therapy Targeted therapy, which uses drugs or other substances that attack specific cancer cells with less harm to normal cells Cancer immunotherapy Hodgkin lymphoma can usually be cured if it is found and treated early."}]}, {"id": "MLP-4627", "title": "Pleural Disorders", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Your pleura is a large, thin sheet of tissue that wraps around the outside of your lungs and lines the inside of your chest cavity."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Between the layers of the pleura is a very thin space."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Normally it's filled with a small amount of fluid."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "The fluid helps the two layers of the pleura glide smoothly past each other as your lungs breathe air in and out."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Disorders of the pleura include: Pleurisy - inflammation of the pleura that causes sharp pain with breathing Pleural effusion - excess fluid in the pleural space Pneumothorax - buildup of air or gas in the pleural space Hemothorax - buildup of blood in the pleural space Many different conditions can cause pleural problems."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Viral infection is the most common cause of pleurisy."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The most common cause of pleural effusion is congestive heart failure ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Lung diseases, like COPD , tuberculosis, and acute lung injury, cause pneumothorax."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Injury to the chest is the most common cause of hemothorax."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Treatment focuses on removing fluid, air, or blood from the pleural space, relieving symptoms, and treating the underlying condition."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1659", "title": "Home Care Services", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Home care is care that allows a person with special needs to stay in their home."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It might be for people who are getting older (aging in place)."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It could also be for people who are chronically ill, recovering from surgery, or have a disability ."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Home care services include: Personal care, such as help with bathing, washing your hair, or getting dressed Household chores, such as cleaning, yard work, and laundry Cooking for you in your home or delivering meals to you Money management, such as help filling out forms and making sure that your bills are paid on time Health care, such as having a home health aide come to your home or getting care from your provider through telehealth You can get almost any type of help you want in your home."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "But some types of care and community services are free or donated."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Sometimes government programs or your health insurance will help cover the cost of certain home care services."}]}]
